Conclusion References License: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license arXiv:2603.05069v3 [cs.AI] 25 Sep 2026 Jagarin: A Three-Layer Architecture for Hibernating Personal Duty Agents on Mobile Ravi Kiran Kadaboina Independent Researcher Jagarin - Sanskrit for wakeful, awake, vigilant Abstract Personal AI agents face a deployment paradox on mobile: persistent background execution drains the battery and conflicts with platform background limits, yet purely reactive agents miss time-sensitive obligations until the user remembers to ask. We present Jagarin , a three-layer architecture that resolves this through structured hibernation and demand-driven wake. DAWN (Duty-Aware Wake Network) is an on-device scoring engine that runs on the platform’s periodic wake and combines four signals (duty-typed optimal action windows, predicted user engagement, the cost of delay, and cross-duty batching) with per-duty adaptive thresholds to decide whether a sleeping agent should stay silent, nudge the user, or offer escalation. ARIA (Agent Relay Identity Architecture) is a commercial email identity proxy that turns institutional email into structured duty records and routes messages by category, removing manual data entry. ACE (Agent-Centric Exchange) is a protocol for machine-readable communication from institutions to personal agents, intended to make email parsing unnecessary in the long run. DAWN and ACE are specified and evaluated in companion papers; this paper describes how the three layers fit together and a working Flutter prototype on Android that combines them with an ephemeral cloud agent invoked only when the user asks. Behavioural signals, thresholds and scoring never leave the device, and every record ARIA extracts is sealed to the device’s public key before it is stored, so the relay holds only ciphertext it cannot read. Cloud model exposure is limited to parsing commercial email and to user-initiated escalation, which receives only the structured duty record. 1. Introduction The promise of personal AI agents managing everyday obligations (insurance renewals, prescription refills, appointment follow-ups, subscription expirations) is well understood. The deployment reality is not. Existing reminder systems answer the wrong question. They ask: how close is the deadline? The right question is: what is the cost of not acting right now, for this person, at this moment? A car insurance renewal 45 days away might be urgent today (competing quotes take time to gather) and a poor use of attention tomorrow morning (the user has back-to-back meetings). A prescription refill 14 days before running out might be the worst thing to raise on a busy Monday and the best on a Saturday when the user passes the pharmacy. Existing personal agent platforms fit mobile poorly for four related reasons: 1. Execution model mismatch. Persistent background agents conflict with iOS and Android background-execution limits. Android WorkManager [1] and iOS BGTaskScheduler [2] provide controlled wake windows, but to our knowledge no prior agent framework models whether action is worthwhile at a given wake. 2. Cold-start dependency. Duty-aware agents need structured obligation data. No user manually enters “insurance renews October 15, optimal action window opens September 5.” Without automatic duty discovery, agents have nothing to reason over. 3. Communication layer mismatch. Institutional communications (receipts, renewal notices, confirmations) are designed for human eyes. An agent receiving an HTML email that says “Your policy renews soon” cannot reliably extract a deadline, a reference number, an optimal action window, or what it is allowed to do next. 4. Alignment mismatch. An agent deployed by an institution optimises for that institution’s objectives, not the user’s. An insurer’s own app will remind you to renew with that insurer; it has no reason to compare competitor quotes. A retailer’s rewards agent surfaces the redemption paths that maximise engagement with that retailer, not the ones with the highest value to the user. If twenty institutions each deploy a per-app agent, all twenty decide independently when to interrupt the user, with no shared interrupt budget. Jagarin is user-deployed; its optimisation target is user value. Jagarin addresses the four problems with one layer each, plus the prototype that joins them. Each layer is independently deployable. Contributions: • DAWN : a multi-signal heuristic for deciding, at each platform wake, whether a hibernating agent should act, framed as opportunity-cost minimisation over duty-typed value curves (§3; full specification and evaluation in [9]) • ARIA : a commercial identity proxy that turns institutional email into duty records and routes the commercial inbox by message category, so that promotions do not flood the duty registry (§4) • ACE : a protocol for direct institution-to-agent communication, filling the gap between human-targeted and transaction-targeted protocols (§5; full specification in [10]) • Jagarin : a working prototype that combines the three layers on Android with an ephemeral cloud escalation path (§6) All institutions named in the examples are fictional. 2. System Architecture The three layers are vertically integrated but independently separable: Figure 1: Jagarin three-layer system architecture. Institutions feed ARIA via email today and ACE in future; ARIA classifies messages and hands duty records to the on-device DAWN engine via FCM; the ephemeral cloud agent runs only on an explicit user tap. The vertical sub-agents are proposed (§4.5); the prototype runs ARIA as a single backend. Cross-duty resonance is computed on the device. Key architectural properties: • Behaviour stays on the device. DAWN scores, thresholds, interaction history and the engagement signals behind BEP are computed and stored only on the device, in an encrypted Hive database whose key is held in the platform keystore. None of it is transmitted. • Sealed relay. ARIA encrypts every record it extracts to the device’s public key before storing it, so it holds only ciphertext it cannot open, and deletes it once the device has it (§4.4). The push that wakes the device carries only an opaque identifier. • Scoped model exposure. ARIA’s Tier-2 parser sends commercial email to a cloud LLM (Gemini 2.5 Flash). This is a deliberate trade-off: the dedicated ARIA address receives only institutional traffic, which is less sensitive than personal correspondence. The escalation agent receives only the structured duty record, sent by the device with the request, and keeps nothing. • No continuous background execution. Android WorkManager wakes DAWN periodically (15-minute minimum) and a high-priority push wakes it when a duty arrives, but Android defers periodic work for rarely opened apps (App Standby Buckets). The deadline reminder therefore does not depend on those wakes: the app books each duty’s urgency-floor reminder with the operating system’s alarm manager, which delivers it on time when the user permits exact alarms and otherwise possibly later, by up to a day once a restricted app’s daily alarm quota is used (§6.1). The periodic wakes decide the earlier nudges. Only Android has been tested; iOS BGTaskScheduler grants wakes at the system’s discretion. 3. DAWN: Duty-Aware Wake Network DAWN is specified and evaluated in the companion paper [9]; this section summarises what the architecture relies on. At each platform wake, DAWN scores every registered duty and returns one of SLEEP, NUDGE, ACT NOW or OVERDUE. It does not schedule wake-ups itself. Signals. Each signal lies in [0, 1]. The Temporal Opportunity Curve (TOC) encodes the fact that every duty type has an optimal action window before its deadline. With t t the days remaining, TOC is an asymmetric Gaussian that peaks at a duty-type centre μ τ \mu_{\tau} , with width σ R \sigma_{R} on the early side and σ L \sigma_{L} on the urgent side: TOC ⁡ ( t , τ ) = { exp ⁡ ( − ( t − μ τ ) 2 2 ​ σ R 2 ) , t ≥ μ τ (early side) exp ⁡ ( − ( t − μ τ ) 2 2 ​ σ L 2 ) , t < μ τ (urgent side) \mathrm{TOC}(t,\tau)\;=\;\begin{cases}\exp\!\left(-\dfrac{(t-\mu_{\tau})^{2}}{2\sigma_{R}^{2}}\right),&t\geq\mu_{\tau}\quad\text{(early side)}\\[8.61108pt] \exp\!\left(-\dfrac{(t-\mu_{\tau})^{2}}{2\sigma_{L}^{2}}\right),&t<\mu_{\tau}\quad\text{(urgent side)}\end{cases} An obligation 45 days out can therefore score higher than one 5 days out, if the first is inside its window and the second has already lost its leverage. The other three signals are: • Behavioural Engagement Predictor (BEP). The probability that the user responds to a notification now, estimated on the device from hour of day, day of week, charging and Wi-Fi state, the recent ignore streak, and hours since the app was last opened. • Value Decay Integral (VDI). The rate at which waiting destroys value: zero while the user is still approaching the window, positive once the peak has passed. The implementation takes a one-day difference of TOC and clips it at zero, so VDI never lowers the composite. • Cross-Duty Resonance (CDR). A batching bonus when another active duty shares a counterparty, an overlapping window or an agent capability, so one session can handle both (“your auto and home insurance both renew within six weeks”). CDR is unavailable to per-app agents: an insurer’s app sees the auto policy it issued, not the home policy held elsewhere. Only an agent that holds duties across counterparties can see the overlap. Composite and decisions. The composite score is S = 0.35 ​ TOC + 0.25 ​ BEP + 0.25 ​ VDI + 0.15 ​ CDR . S=0.35\,\mathrm{TOC}+0.25\,\mathrm{BEP}+0.25\,\mathrm{VDI}+0.15\,\mathrm{CDR}. Two per-duty thresholds θ 1 < θ 2 \theta^{1}<\theta^{2} divide it into SLEEP ( S < θ 1 S<\theta^{1} ), NUDGE ( θ 1 ≤ S < θ 2 \theta^{1}\leq S<\theta^{2} ) and ACT NOW ( S ≥ θ 2 S\geq\theta^{2} ). ACT NOW makes the cloud agent available; escalation itself is always user-initiated. Within a duty-type urgency floor before the deadline the decision is forced to ACT NOW, and past the deadline it is OVERDUE. Duties that need the user’s physical presence, such as a buy-online-pick-up-in-store order, are capped at NUDGE, including at the urgency floor, since no cloud agent can substitute for being there. Adaptive thresholds. Thresholds adapt per duty with a simple step rule: each response to a notification lowers both thresholds by α \alpha , and each ignored notification raises both by α \alpha , with α = 0.05 \alpha=0.05 , bounds [ 0.15 , 0.75 ] [0.15,0.75] , a minimum gap of 0.05 and a ceiling of 0.55 on θ 1 \theta^{1} ; initial values are ( 0.30 , 0.65 ) (0.30,0.65) . The rule settles where the user responds to half of the notifications that fire. This rule corrects the threshold update given in earlier versions of this paper. Two users with identical duties may therefore be reminded on different days. A user who answers every nudge drives both thresholds to their floor and is nudged earlier, which is the intent; how often they are notified is bounded separately by the notification policy (§6), which shows at most one notification per duty per day whatever the thresholds are. Evidence and limits. BEP is calibrated in [9] on a public dataset of 3.4 million notification events from 342 users [11]: a logistic model reaches a test AUC of 0.69, against 0.62 for the rule-based heuristic. The dataset is mostly social and messaging notifications, so transfer to institutional duties is a working hypothesis. BEP and the thresholds only shift when within the window a duty surfaces; the urgency floor ignores both, so neither can suppress a reminder before the deadline. A user who keeps ignoring nudges about a long-window duty is next notified only at the urgency floor [9]. 4. ARIA: Agent Relay Identity Architecture DAWN needs structured duty data, and manual entry is impractical. ARIA solves the cold-start problem by converting institutional email into duties automatically. 4.1 Commercial Identity Separation ARIA gives the user a dedicated agent email address (for example user@aria.example ) that is handed only to commercial entities. The user’s personal inbox receives only intentional correspondence, and the agent address receives only commercial traffic, which is what makes cloud parsing of it an acceptable trade-off (§2). 4.2 Purchase Pattern Model (PPM) and Social Pattern Model (SPM) Every invoice and receipt flowing through ARIA can be parsed into a Purchase Pattern Model: a private, on-device record of what the user buys, from whom, how often and at what price point. Marketing email is scored against it: an offer in a category the user bought from recently scores high, an unsolicited brand promotion scores near zero, and offers below threshold are archived without notifying the user. PPM is the relevance signal the DAWN composite [9] uses for a Commercial Opportunity: PPM = 0.45·category_affinity + 0.25·counterparty_loyalty + 0.20·price_band_match + 0.10·seasonal_match Each sub-score lies in [0, 1] and is computed from the on-device purchase graph: recency-weighted purchases in the offer’s category (90-day decay), the share of the user’s purchases in that category made with the sender, closeness of the offer’s price tier to the user’s usual tier, and a seasonal match. The Social Pattern Model is the parallel signal for Social/Platform Updates, weighting how often the user opens the platform (0.40), responds to that content type (0.35) and recognises the author (0.25). DAWN’s 0.35 / 0.25 / 0.25 / 0.15 allocation is the Temporal Obligation composite; the other categories use their own weights with these relevance signals added: Category TOC BEP VDI CDR PPM SPM Temporal Obligation 0.35 0.25 0.25 0.15 n/a n/a Commercial Opportunity 0.10 0.15 0.05 0.10 0.60 n/a Rewards (with expiry) 0.30 0.10 0.30 0.10 0.20 n/a Social Update 0.05 0.25 n/a n/a n/a 0.70 PPM, SPM and these weights are a specification: the prototype does not yet compute them and gives every commercial message a relevance of 1.0. 4.3 Category Routing ARIA does not register every commercial message as a duty. It routes by category: Category Examples ARIA action DAWN integration Temporal Obligation Insurance renewal, subscription expiry, store pickup, return deadline Extract deadline and optimal window, register a duty record Full TOC, VDI and CDR scoring Commercial Opportunity Flash sales, weekend promotions, personalised offers PPM relevance score Store and notify at low priority if relevant; otherwise archive Rewards Signal Points balance, tier upgrade, points expiry warning Check for an expiry date and redeemable value Register a duty if both are present; otherwise update the rewards record Social/Platform Update Follower milestones, community activity Engagement score at ingest Notify if relevant; no duty registered The taxonomy mirrors ACE’s message categories (§5) and keeps promotional volume out of the duty registry: an insurance renewal and a flash sale are structurally different even when both arrive by email. ACE defines a fifth category, Security Alert, which bypasses scoring and interrupts the user by priority class; ARIA does not route it yet, so such an email arrives as an ordinary item. 4.4 Automatic Duty Ingestion ARIA first classifies each message: Gemini 2.5 Flash chooses the category, treating any email that states a deadline the recipient must meet as an obligation even if it also advertises, with keyword rules as the offline fallback. Obligations go to the Tier-2 parser (Gemini 2.5 Flash), with the Tier-1 keyword and regular-expression parser as the fallback; the other categories use Tier-1 only. PDF attachments are converted to text and appended to the parsing context. For an obligation ARIA then: 1. Extracts the counterparty, deadline, optimal action window, reference number, value at stake and escalation capability 2. Builds a DAWN duty record 3. Seals the record to the device’s public key, stores only the ciphertext, and wakes the device with a Firebase Cloud Messaging data message that carries only an opaque identifier 4. The device fetches and decrypts the record, stores it in its encrypted registry and acknowledges it, and ARIA deletes the ciphertext; periodic sync is the fallback No user action is needed between receipt and registration. For rewards messages received through ACE with an expiry date and a redeemable value above USD 5.00, the backend registers a duty with a cliff at the expiry, turning a passive balance notice into a tracked obligation. 4.5 Vertical Sub-Agents The prototype uses a single FastAPI backend that performs all routing in-process. A future version could split parsing into vertical sub-agents (Shopping, Health, Services, Grocery) coordinated over A2A [5]. Like the single backend, each would see an email only while parsing it and store only the sealed record, so the sub-agents cannot compare duties with one another; cross-duty resonance stays on the device, the only place that can read every duty. The split is not implemented; the part that is implemented is the category routing that keeps promotions out of the obligation pipeline. 5. ACE: Agent-Centric Exchange Protocol ARIA parses email because institutions write for people. ACE [10] specifies what institutions would send if they wrote for agents. Email (RFC 5321 [7]) and iCalendar (RFC 5545 [8]) assume a human recipient, and agentic-commerce protocols such as UCP [3] cover the point of purchase rather than the ongoing relationship; A2A [5], ACP [4] and MCP [6] address agent-to-agent tasks and tool calls. Every ACE message carries a universal envelope with four core schemas: ACE-TEMP (deadline, urgency class and optional action-window hints, which map directly onto DAWN’s TOC parameters), ACE-VALUE (value at stake), ACE-SCOPE (what the agent may do without asking) and ACE-TRUST (affiliate and recommendation-basis disclosure). Messages fall into five categories, four of which ARIA routes today (§4.3). The companion paper gives a JSON-LD vocabulary, SHACL shapes that make message validity machine-checkable, a TLA+ model of the duty-registration lifecycle and SPARQL query patterns. Each message carries a sender signature, which the receiver verifies only against a key served from the sender’s own domain, so a spoofed message is rejected before it reaches the registry. ACE reuses A2A’s Agent Card for discovery, and an ACE message can also travel inside ordinary email as a structured part, which gives senders an incremental adoption path [10]. 6. Implementation: Jagarin We implemented the three layers in a research prototype, Jagarin , demonstrated on Android (API 26+). It is written in Flutter, but the iOS build has not been tested. Mobile application (Flutter/Dart): • DAWN engine in pure Dart; no network access during scoring • Background execution: WorkManager (15-minute periodic task) plus an FCM wake on ingestion; urgency-floor reminders booked with the alarm manager, one per floor day, exact when the user grants “Alarms & reminders” access and inexact otherwise, re-booked on every change and after a reboot • Notification policy: a duty entering ACT NOW or OVERDUE notifies once and then at most once a day while it stays there; only the top NUDGE per wake is shown, at most once a day per duty • Adaptive thresholds persisted per duty and updated on notification interaction. The prototype implements the step rule and bounds of §3; the gap and ceiling logic, and the calibrated TOC parameters of [9], exist in the reference simulation and have not yet been ported. • UI: duty list with DAWN decision badges and a per-duty score breakdown ARIA backend (Python/FastAPI): • Model-based category classifier and Tier-2 Gemini 2.5 Flash extraction, with keyword and regex rules as the offline fallback • PDF attachment text extraction via PyMuPDF • ACE ingest endpoint ( POST /ace/ingest ) accepting envelopes with the four core schemas; it is protected by an API key and does not yet verify ACE sender signatures • A2A discovery via an Agent Card at GET /.well-known/agent-card.json • Sealed-box encryption of every stored record to the device key (PyNaCl), deletion on acknowledgement, and an opaque FCM wake on ingestion Ephemeral cloud agent: • Invoked only on an explicit user tap; stateless: receives the duty record from the device and returns a recommendation, action points and a draft message • If the duty carries an institution’s action endpoint (from ACE), the agent uses it; otherwise Gemini 2.5 Flash drafts the plan, with a rule-based fallback when no model is available Duty types implemented (12): Insurance Renewal, Prescription Refill, Wellness Visit, Subscription Renewal, Vehicle Service, Return Deadline, License Renewal, Support Follow-up, Tax Deadline, Travel Check-in, Store Pickup, Custom. Figure 2. Duties tab. DAWN decisions appear as badges: vehicle service in 60 days (SLEEP), prescription refill in 22 days (NUDGE), insurance renewal in 7 days (ACT NOW, forced by the urgency floor). Figure 3. Duty detail: the four DAWN signals, the composite score and the duty’s adaptive thresholds, with escalation offered at ACT NOW. Figure 4. Cloud agent result from Gemini 2.5 Flash: the last action points and a draft quote request built only from the duty record the device sent. Screenshots show sample duties seeded with fictional institutions. 6.1 Deadline reminder delivery We checked on an Android emulator, one run per condition, that the booked reminder is delivered when Android throttles the app: after confirming the booking with dumpsys alarm , we moved the app to the restricted App Standby bucket, turned the screen off, forced deep idle (Doze), and read the posted notification’s timestamp. Reminder Delivered Exact (“Alarms & reminders” granted), restricted + deep idle 35 ms after the booked time Inexact (not granted), restricted + deep idle about 4 minutes late, at the end of Android’s batching window Inexact, restricted, that day’s alarm quota already used deferred by App Standby to about 23 hours later (read from dumpsys , not waited out) With the user’s permission the reminder arrived on time in the restricted bucket under deep idle; without it, Android may shift it within its batching window or, once a restricted app’s daily alarm quota is used, to the next day, so the app asks for the permission once at setup. A user force-stop cancels any app’s alarms until the app is opened again. Battery Saver modes and manufacturers’ own battery managers, which can go beyond Android’s rules, were not tested. The procedure and raw dumpsys excerpts are in the research repository ( eval/floor_reminder/ ). 7. Discussion User alignment as a design property. Jagarin is user-deployed rather than institution-deployed, and this is a structural choice. An institution-deployed agent’s hint for an insurance renewal will be “renew with us”; Jagarin’s is “compare the renewal quote against other insurers”. An institution’s notification logic predicts when engagement serves its goals; DAWN’s BEP predicts when the user is receptive. The mechanism that keeps Jagarin aligned is architectural rather than a policy: behavioural data never reaches an institution, no duty state is exposed to counterparties, and the escalation capability comes from the user or from ACE messages the user receives, not from the institution whose product is being evaluated. Privacy and threat model. What the user does (app opens, which nudges they answer, the thresholds learned from that, and every score) is computed and stored only on the device and never transmitted. What institutions send reaches the device through ARIA as a sealed relay: records are encrypted to the device’s public key before storage, the push service sees only an opaque identifier, and the ciphertext is deleted once delivered, so a compromised relay holds nothing readable. ARIA does read each commercial email in memory while parsing it, and the Tier-2 parser sends it to a cloud LLM; we accept this because that address receives only institutional traffic the institution already holds, and an on-device parser would close it. Because anyone can send mail to the ARIA address, extracted fields are treated as untrusted data and nothing is sent to an institution except on an explicit user tap. Platform compliance. DAWN makes no network calls during a wake cycle, and cloud invocation requires a user action, which keeps the design within App Store and Play Store background rules. This has been exercised on Android only. Relation to agent email infrastructure. Since the first version of this paper, email for agents has become a product category: AgentMail [15] and Cloudflare’s Email Service [16] give agents their own programmable inboxes. They supply the first part of ARIA (a dedicated address with inbound hooks) as a service, and an ARIA deployment could use either as its mail transport. They do not decide when a user should be interrupted about what arrives, which is DAWN’s role, and what they carry is still human-oriented email rather than a structured institutional format, which is ACE’s. Relation to agent frameworks. AutoGPT [12], LangGraph [13] and CrewAI [14] assume persistent execution with continuous model access, which does not fit mobile background limits; any of them could back Jagarin’s escalation step. Jagarin’s contribution is the decision about when running any agent is worthwhile, not the agent itself. Limitations. The prototype uses the rule-based BEP; the calibrated model of [9] is not deployed. ARIA’s classification and extraction accuracy have not been measured on a representative corpus. PPM, SPM, the non-obligation weights, Security Alert routing and ACE signature verification are specified but not implemented, and the iOS build is untested. We report no battery measurements. The combined system has not been tested with real users on long-horizon duties, and ACE depends on institutional incentives that have not yet materialised. 8. Conclusion Jagarin shows how a personal duty agent can work within mobile platform limits: it hibernates between platform wakes, keeps duty state and behavioural signals on the device, and uses cloud models only to parse commercial email and, when the user asks, to draft an action plan. DAWN decides when a duty deserves the user’s attention, ARIA turns today’s institutional email into duties, and ACE describes the structured channel that would make that parsing unnecessary. DAWN and ACE are specified and evaluated in [9] and [10]. The main open work for the architecture as a whole is measuring ARIA’s extraction on a multi-user corpus and testing the combined system with real users over long-horizon duties. The DAWN and ACE research artifacts (simulation, calibration, TLA+ model, SHACL shapes and tests) are available at https://github.com/ravikiran438/jagarin-research .
